# Task graph: parents, links, and the ready query

Task-system phase P2 (design record `fm3000-task-system-design-s1/report.md`, sections 7 to 9). P0 made a task a durable record, P1 made every captain ask land on one; P2 gives the records structure - one parent per task, typed links between them - and turns the R1 sweep into a query over that structure.

## The graph

- **Hierarchy**: `tasks.parent_id`, one parent per task. A child inherits its parent's project (and its repo unless bound to one of its own); the ancestor walk refuses a cycle at write time (`TaskService.setParent`). A parent may carry a crewmate or be a pure container - a planned row that never dispatches on its own.
- **Links** (`task_links`, primary key `(from, to, type)`): `blocks` - `to` is not ready until `from` closes successfully (delivered or done; dropped never clears); `related` - informational; `discovered-from` - `from` was found while doing `to`, no readiness effect. A `blocks` edge that would close a cycle is refused at insert (`TaskGraphRefusal`, surfaced as tool text): the walk follows `blocks` edges outward from `to` and must not reach `from`.
- **Derived, never stored** (design principle 4): `blocked`, `held`, `ready`, `deadBlocker` come from `TaskService.flagsOf` at read time.

## The ready query

`TaskStore.listReady()` is the sweep's dispatch list: open work, no gate, `start_policy = when-ready`, no `blocks` edge from a task that is not delivered or done; priority first, then age. `CrewSupervisor.sweepGates` runs it on the shared 60 s tick, after any close (`closeTask` and `finish` both sweep), after any graph change (`graphChanged`), on quota refresh, and once at boot. On-request rows never appear in it; a captain-held row waits on its card.

A row whose blocker was **dropped** is a wait that cannot end: `listDeadBlocked` feeds the existing dead-gate decision card ("A wait cannot end") with three answers - keep waiting (Later: the card parks and returns), drop it too, start anyway - and parks the row on a captain hold so the query stops listing it. Removing the dead edge with `link_tasks remove` lifts the hold and retires the card (`reconcileDeadGate`).

## The parent close rule

A parent closes only when every child is closed (`TaskService.closeRefusal` names the open children by key). `settle_task` in every mode, `landTask`, and `mergePrTask` check it first and return the refusal as text. `update_task drop` on a parent with open children needs `confirm`, which drops the open descendants as `superseded` (deepest first) and then the parent as `cancelled`; work a crewmate holds or delivered is never dropped from a field edit - that stays with settle_task and its unlanded-work guard. Host closes (a failed turn, a cancel) are unguarded by design: a record must always be able to record what happened to it.

## Tools

Firstmate (`src/core/pi/taskTools.ts`): `create_task` (plan without starting: intent, `parent`, `blocked_by`, `start_policy` defaulting to on-request, `priority`), `update_task` (title, goal, priority, start_policy, parent, project for open workspace-less work, or `drop` with `reason` and `confirm`), `link_tasks` (`from`, `to`, `type`, `remove`), and `tasks` (the query: project, status, key, text, parent). `spawn_crewmate` gained `parent`, `blocked_by`, and `priority`; `after_task` stays as an alias of `blocked_by`. Every write attaches the turn's ask to the task it acts on (P1's attach-first). The prompt's class 4 is "spawn or plan"; the C5 dispatch extractor sorts `create_task` with spawn, the graph edits with operate, and `tasks` with the reads.

Crewmates (`src/core/pi/crewmateTaskTools.ts`, the same pair over Claude's tool server in `src/core/claude/claudeTaskTools.ts`; Cursor has no tool surface): `file_followup` (title, goal, why, `blocks_me`) files an on-request child of the crewmate's own task with a `discovered-from` edge, inheriting project and repo, and the Firstmate hears one `[fm-op]` that names the key and the choices; `note_progress` writes one `progress` event on the crewmate's own timeline with `feed = 0`. Both register through `CrewmateSpec.onFollowup` / `onProgress`.

The supervision session gets the read-only `tasks` query beside `crew_status`, so a wake about a task can see its parent, blockers, and follow-ups; it still writes nothing on the graph.

## Context block

Index rows carry the graph in a few words: `[under SCR-1; blocked by SCR-3]`, `[on request]`, `blocked by X (dropped)`. `crew_status` says `starts on request` for a planned row.

arguments.title: Why finished work is labeled delivered
arguments.body:
Keep delivered. Neither idle nor waiting is a better stored status. Idle is the quiet crewmate; waiting is the captain’s open question. Delivered is finished work whose worktree is still there.

Three layers, not one word

LayerValuesMeans
Statusopen · active · delivered · done · droppedRecord lifecycle
Activitystarting · running · idle · interruptedOnly while active: what the crewmate is doing
Now groupwaiting on you · underway · to land · charted · landedCaptain-facing words

Pre-P0 used one enum (queued / running / idle / interrupted / completed). Idle split into activity; completed split into delivered (worktree present) vs done (worktree gone). That split is still the rule in mapLegacyStatus and close().

Status, what writes it, what you see

StatusWhenClosed?Captain word
openPlanned; not started. Gates, blockers, on-request live here.nocharted, blocked, held, on request, or waiting on you
activeA crewmate has it. Activity says if it is starting, running, idle, or interrupted.nounderway, idle, interrupted, or waiting on you
deliveredCrewmate decommissioned after a report. Worktree stays until land or discard. Closed reason is finished.yes, but still live on the boardto land
doneLanded, merged, answered, or settled. Worktree gone.yesdone / answered
droppedCancelled, discarded, failed, superseded.yesdropped / failed (off the panel)

Finish requires the runtime to be idle, then writes delivered. Keep on a settle card does the opposite: the card goes away and the crewmate stays idle and active. Same quiet worker, two different records.

Delivered is closed enough that blockers clear and the crew is gone, and live enough that the board, listLive, and the live query still show it. That in-between is the point of the word.

Where idle and waiting already live

  • Idle — active activity; runtime between turns; crew-strip idle count; Observe session; keep-after-settle.
  • Waiting — now-panel group for needs-you (open decision card, captain hold, dead blocker); crew-strip parked decisions; waitingCardId.

Needs-you is derived and never stored. Protocol sets it only on open/active rows, so a delivered row is to-land, not waiting on you, even though land/discard still needs a person.

Other axes (not status)

  • Kind: work, question, decision, operation
  • Start policy: when-ready, on-request
  • Gate: quota-reset, at-time, captain
  • Flags: blocked, held, ready, needsYou
  • Workspace: none, present, removed
  • Closed reason: landed, merged, answered, settled, finished, cancelled, discarded, failed, superseded

If renamed to idle

  • Collides with activity idle: finish today is “idle, therefore write delivered.” One word would cover “between turns” and “decommissioned with a worktree.”
  • Keep vs Done would no longer be distinguishable on the record.
  • Ready query, wire schema, board counts, Observe (delivered → done), character emotes on task_changed, and every SQLite row would need a migration.

If renamed to waiting

  • Collides with waiting on you. Delivered rows do not have needsYou.
  • The panel would have a status named waiting and a group named waiting that do not mean the same thing.
  • Same protocol, SQL, and migration blast radius as idle.

What is a bit muddy, and not worth a rename: Firstmate’s index still prints “delivered,” tools say “finished,” the card says “to land.” Same state, three words. Display alignment would be enough if that bothers you.

arguments.title: Who writes delivered, and how active would stick
arguments.body:
Deterministic host code writes the status. Neither Firstmate nor a crewmate can set status to a string. The one writer is TaskService.close in src/core/tasks/taskService.ts (around 1048). Agents only choose a tool or a card action; the supervisor maps that onto close.

The mapping

CrewSupervisor.closeRecord in src/core/orchestrator/crewSupervisor.ts (1986–1993) is the only product path that asks for delivered:

  • wire completed → stored delivered, reason finished
  • cancelled / failed → dropped

Opening a PR does not do this. PrCiService.record in src/core/orchestrator/prCi.ts (210–232) only patches delivery.prUrl / delivery.ci via recordDelivery. CI pending is a delivery fact on whatever status the row already has.

What can trigger completed → delivered

  1. settle_task mode finish — Firstmate tool in src/core/pi/crewTools.ts (256–268), wired in firstmateAgent.ts (747–749), handled at settleTaskOnce (1819–1824). The agent picks finish; the host decommissions. No CI check.
  2. Done on a task-result card — act() (2910–2918) and taskCardActions (3114–3118). Captain click; host calls finish(..., "completed"). No CI check.
  3. Cancel on an idle crewmate that already reported — interruptCrewmate (1144–1148, 1162–1163) plus idleCancelStatus (1181–1182). Treated as decommission, not abort.
  4. finish() itself (1581–1582) when the runtime is torn down while the row is still open or active.

Keep on a settle card does not write delivered. act() (2920–2923) leaves the crewmate idle and the record active.

Migration and test fixtures also map old completed → delivered when a worktree exists (src/core/storage/db.ts mapLegacyStatus, src/core/tasks/seedTask.ts). Not a live path.

How “change it to active” would work

We would not add a “set status active” tool, and we would not ask the agent to pick a status. Active is the default while a crewmate exists. The change is: do not call closeRecord(..., "completed") on a direct-pr row whose delivery.ci is pending, red, or unchecked.

  • Finish / Done / idle-cancel would refuse with text, same as finish already refuses a streaming crewmate (1822–1824). The row stays active because it never closed.
  • Firstmate would keep steering (prompt already says not-green → steer, no captain card: src/core/pi/piResources.ts ~82). That is policy on top of the gate, not a second writer.
  • Merge-pr and discard stay as they are. Merge already re-checks CI in PrCiService.merge.
  • Rows already delivered with ci pending would not be auto-reopened. Display-only: taskStatusWord in src/shared/nowPanel.ts would say CI pending instead of to land. Reopening is a different, larger change.

Nothing will be edited until you approve a change.

arguments.title: Cancel left FI3-55 in to land
arguments.body:
Yes. Firstmate was stopping a corrupted crewmate. The runtime did go away. The record was closed as delivered, so the worktree stayed and the now panel listed it under to land.

What actually tore down

interruptCrewmate cancel on an idle runtime calls finish, which disposes the transport and drops it from the live map (crewSupervisor.ts 1570–1582). Crewmate 6 was gone. That is the process teardown.

The record is a different object. idleCancelStatus (1181–1182) saw the garbled lastCompleteText and returned completed. closeRecord then wrote delivered / finished. Delivered means “decommissioned, worktree still there,” which the panel prints as to land. finish never calls closeTask, so the worktree is not removed on this path.

The host comment at 1173–1178 says this on purpose: cancel on an idle crewmate that already reported is treated as decommission, because Firstmate sometimes uses cancel after a merge. After a real merge the row is already done and cancel is a no-op (1142). The upgrade is leftover. A junk report is enough to trigger it, which is FI3-55.

The persist-only branch is the same idea, worse: idle activity alone becomes completed (1146–1148), even with no report.

How to avoid it

Host path only. Do not ask the agent to pick a status. Cancel must never call closeRecord(..., "completed").

  1. Delete idleCancelStatus. Idle cancel always finish(task, "cancelled") → dropped / cancelled.
  2. Persist-only cancel: always cancelled, never activity === "idle" ? "completed".
  3. Decommission that keeps a worktree stays on settle_task finish only.
  4. Flip the two tests that currently require cancel-after-report to be completed (crewSupervisor.test.ts ~397 and ~456).

Dropped rows leave the now panel (to land goes away). finish(cancelled) still leaves the worktree on disk. For a full stop, cancel should go through closeTask({ status: "dropped", reason: "cancelled" }), which already removes the worktree. That is the stronger teardown; the mapping change is the minimum that stops to land.

Nothing will be edited until you approve.

arguments.body:
Settled proposal, now matching the host change:

  • interrupt_crewmate cancel always closes cancelled/dropped. A report, including a garbled one, does not upgrade that to delivered. That is the FI3-55 path.
  • settle_task finish is still the decommission that keeps a worktree (delivered / to land).
  • No extra worktree teardown on cancel. Dropped rows leave the now panel; the worktree can remain on disk.
  • Already delivered or done stays as-is if cancel is called again.
